title: Directed Differentiation of Functional Astroglial Subtypes from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells
markdown:
## Protocol: Protocol for directed differentiation and long-term maintenance of functional astroglial subtypes from human pluripotent stem cells

### Overview

This protocol outlines the directed differentiation and long-term maintenance of functional astroglial subtypes from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs). The process involves neural induction, regional patterning using morphogens (RA, SHH), expansion of neuroepithelial spheres, transition to gliogenic astrospheres via EGF/FGF2 treatment, and subsequent maturation into monolayer astrocytes. Key timepoints include Days 10-21 for patterning, Days 21-90 for sphere expansion and gliogenic switch, and Day 90 for verification of astroglial progenitors. Optional branches include freezing/thawing cells, immunocytochemistry for quality control, and detailed maturation protocols.

### Materials/Reagents

- Neural Medium (NM): D-MEM/F-12, NEAA, N-2 supplement, heparin
- Heparin (20 mg/ml stock)
- Epidermal Growth Factor (EGF, 100 μg/ml stock)
- Fibroblast Growth Factor 2 (FGF2, 100 μg/ml stock)
- Sonic Hedgehog (SHH, 100 μg/ml stock)
- Retinoic Acid (RA, 100 mM in DMSO, 1 mM in ethanol working solution)
- Poly-L-ornithine (PLO, 1 mg/ml stock)
- Laminin
- Paraformaldehyde (PFA, 4% wt/vol)
- Accutase
- Freezing media
- CNTF (Ciliary Neurotrophic Factor)

### Equipment

- Phase contrast microscope
- CO2 incubator (37°C, 5% CO2, humidified)
- 24-well plates
- T25 flasks
- 15-ml conical tubes
- Centrifuge
- Flamed, curved Pasteur pipettes (aperture 0.2-0.5 mm)
- Steriflip filters
- Cryogenic vials
- -80°C freezer
- Liquid nitrogen storage
- 37°C water bath
- Hemocytometer

### Safety & Sterility

- Retinoic acid is light-sensitive; keep protected from light.
- Paraformaldehyde (PFA) is hazardous: avoid skin contact, eye contact, ingestion, and inhalation. Use in a fume hood. Overexposure can lead to death.
- Acid etching of coverslips requires concentrated nitric acid; handle with extreme caution.
- Maintain sterile conditions during all cell culture steps, including coating coverslips and handling aggregates.
- Flame polish Pasteur pipettes carefully to ensure smooth edges and appropriate aperture size to prevent cell damage.

## Reagent Preparation

### Pre-experiment Setup

1. Prepare Neural Medium (NM, 500 ml) by combining 490 ml of D-MEM/F-12, 5 ml of NEAA, 5 ml of N-2 supplement, and 50 μl of heparin. Store at 4°C for up to 2 weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare Heparin (20 mg/ml) by dissolving 20 mg into 1 ml of D-MEM/F-12. Aliquot and store at −80°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare Epidermal growth factor (EGF, 100 μg/ml) by dissolving 200 μg into 2 ml of sterile D-PBS. Aliquot and store at −80°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Prepare Fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2, 100 μg/ml) by dissolving 25 μg into 250 μl of sterile D-PBS. Aliquot and store at −80°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
5. Prepare Sonic hedgehog (SHH, 100 μg/ml) by dissolving 25 μg into 250 μl of sterile D-PBS to create a 100 μg/ml stock. Aliquot and store at −80°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
6. Prepare Retinoic acid (RA). Dissolve 30 mg into 1 ml of DMSO to create a 100 mM stock solution; aliquot and store at −20°C. Before use, dilute 50 μl of the 100 mM stock into 5 ml ethanol to create a 1 mM working solution; store at −20°C for up to 2 weeks. Critical: Keep RA protected from light as it is light sensitive. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
7. Prepare Polyornithine (PLO, 1 mg/ml) by dissolving 100 mg into 100 ml of boric acid buffer (pH 8.4). Filter with a Steriflip and store at −20°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->
8. Prepare Paraformaldehyde (PFA, 4% wt/vol). Dissolve 220 mg sodium phosphate monobasic and 1.22 g sodium phosphate dibasic into 50 ml water. In a fume hood, add 4 g PFA to 50 ml of 60°C water while stirring. Add 2-3 drops of 2N NaOH to dissolve. Combine the two solutions and cool to 22°C. Adjust pH to 7.4 with HCl, filter with a Steriflip, and store at 4°C for up to two weeks. Caution: PFA is very hazardous in case of skin contact, eye contact, ingestion, and inhalation leading to irritation. Over exposure can lead to death. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S08 -->
9. Set cell culture incubation conditions: Set the incubator at 37°C and connect to a CO2 tank for a final concentration of 5%. Add water for humid conditions. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S09 -->
10. Prepare PLO and laminin coated coverslips. Acid etch coverslips by overnight shaking in concentrated nitric acid, followed by 8 washes with distilled water over 24 hours. Insert acid-etched coverslips into each well of a 24-well plate in sterile conditions. Add 0.5 ml of ethanol to each well to sterilize, and after evaporation, wash 2 times with sterile water. Dilute the PLO stock solution 1:10 into sterile water. Add 75 μl of diluted PLO onto each coverslip and store in an incubator overnight. Remove PLO, dry for 30 minutes, followed by 3 water washes. Dry again and store at −20°C for up to one month. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S10 -->
11. One hour before use, dilute 25 μl of laminin solution into 1.25 ml of NM and add 50 μl onto each of the PLO-treated coverslips. Do not let the solution spread off the coverslip onto the edge of the well. Store in an incubator for at least 1 hour prior to plating cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S11 -->

## Procedure

### Days 10-21

1. Observe the neural differentiation culture under a phase contrast scope. The attached neuroepithelial cell colonies should form a uniform multilayer of cells. If cells become single layer or dark clusters of dead cells appear, mechanically remove and dispense the clusters. Feed the culture with fresh media every 2-3 days, exchanging half of the media. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Without morphogen addition, human PSC-derived neural cells exhibit dorsal telencephalic characteristics. To generate astrocytes of different regional identities, add morphogens starting at day 10 of neuroepithelial cell differentiation. Add RA (1:2,000 dilution for 0.5 μM) or SHH (1:1,000-1:200 dilution for 100-500 ng/ml) to NM to caudalize or ventralize progenitor cells, respectively, or use a combination for caudal/ventral cells. These molecules must be continuously present in the NM until day 21 for complete patterning. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->

### Days 21-90

1. On day 21, replace media with NM + EGF and FGF2 (10 ng/ml each) to expand the spheres. Morphogens are no longer necessary at this late stage for regional patterning. Replace 75% of media every 2-3 days. Discard spheres that are tightly attached to the flask during exchange of new flasks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
2. During days 21-90, break any large spheres into multiple smaller clusters. Take large spheres into a flamed, curved Pasteur pipette rinsed with media at least three times to avoid attachment to the pipette wall. Force the spheres out once or twice. A detailed procedure for making these pipettes has been described elsewhere. Critical: Care should be taken to flame polish the Pasteur pipette to smooth edges and achieve an appropriate aperture (0.2-0.5 mm in diameter), as a more narrow opening will cause excessive damage and cell death. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Critical: Care should be taken to flame polish the Pasteur pipette to smooth edges and achieve an appropriate aperture (0.2-0.5 mm in diameter), as a more narrow opening will cause excessive damage and cell death. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S03 -->
3. During days 21-90, break any large spheres into multiple smaller clusters. To break spheres, take large spheres into a flamed, curved Pasteur pipette that has been rinsed with media at least three times to avoid attachment of spheres to the wall of the pipette. Then force the spheres out once or twice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T4-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** A detailed procedure for making these pipettes has been described elsewhere. Critical: Care should be taken to flame polish the Pasteur pipette to smooth edges and achieve an appropriate aperture (0.2-0.5 mm in diameter), as a more narrow opening will cause excessive damage and cell death. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T4-S02 -->
4. Between days 21-90, the EGF/FGF2-expanded and regularly triturated progenitor clusters will switch from neurogenic to gliogenic, and these aggregates are referred to as astrospheres. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T4-S03 -->

### day 90

1. Between days 21-90, the EGF/FGF2-expanded and regularly triturated progenitor clusters will switch from neurogenic to gliogenic, and these aggregates are referred to as astrospheres. At day 90, verify the efficiency of gliogenesis by immunostaining. Expected outcome: ~80% of cells are S100β+, ~80% are CD44+, and ~10% are GFAP+. These cells are regarded as astroglial progenitors/immature astrocytes. At this stage, proceed to Step 10, or perform optional steps: attaching monolayers of astroglial progenitors for maturation and experimentation (Option A), immunostaining for cell type confirmation (Option B), or freeze/thawing cells for storage (Box 1). Commonly, most cells are further expanded to generate large quantities of astrocytes (Step 10) whilst a small proportion is fixed for immunocytochemistry to track the differentiation process. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->
2. By day 90, astrospheres are primarily composed of cells with the ability to generate S100β+ immature astrocytes. Up to this stage, cells are maintained as spheres to easily select out any non-neural cells that attach to the flask. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T6-S01 -->

### Freezing and Thawing

#### Branch A: Freezing

1. i. At any time point along the astroglial differentiation, cells can be frozen in liquid nitrogen for future use as dissociated cells or as astrospheres. Transfer cells to be frozen from one flask to a 15-ml tube and centrifuge at 100g. ii. Remove the supernatant and resuspend by slowly adding freezing media. iii. Transfer the cell suspension to cryogenic vials and store overnight at −80°C within a freezing container. The next day, store vials in liquid nitrogen. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S01 -->

#### Branch B: Thawing

1. iv. For thawing cells, remove vials from liquid nitrogen and immediately place in a 37°C water bath. v. Transfer cell suspension to a 15-ml tube and wash by slowly adding 10 ml NM prewarmed to 37°C. Centrifuge at 100g and remove supernatant. vi. Resuspend cells with NM + EGF + FGF2 and continuously culture in a flask as previously described. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S02 -->

### Maturation of astrocytes

#### Branch A: Maturation

1. i. Prepare a 24-well plate containing PLO and laminin-coated coverslips as described in equipment setup. Without laminin, cells will attach but do not flatten out on the glass, making proper detection of proteins difficult. Alternatively, 1% serum may be added in the initial plating (<24 hours) to induce attachment. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S01 -->
2. ii. Transfer ~50 astrospheres to a 15-ml tube. Centrifuge at 100g, remove the supernatant, and digest with 0.5 ml of prewarmed Accutase at 37°C for 5 minutes. Immediately wash 2X with prewarmed D-MEM/F-12 to remove Accutase. Resuspend with 1 ml of NM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S02 -->
3. iii. Break astrospheres into single cells by triturating through a small pipette tip 3-5 times. Critical: If clusters still remain, they may be transferred to a second tube for additional trituration with ~50 μl of solution, and then returned to the original tube. This allows for full dissociation of clusters, while avoiding excessive trituration of dissociated cells, which may cause cell death. Count the number of single live cells using a standard hemocytometer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S03 -->
4. iv. For one 24-well plate containing laminin-coated coverslips, resuspend 240,000 cells into 1.2 ml of NM and add 50 μl directly onto each coverslip containing 50 μl of laminin solution, for a plating density of 10,000 cells/cm². Do not allow the cell suspension to spill out of the coverslip. If fewer cells are obtained after digestion, recalculate to maintain a similar plating density for fewer coverslips. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S04 -->
5. v. Cells will attach between 3-5 hours after plating. After attachment, carefully add 0.5 ml of NM + CNTF (10 ng/ml) to each well and change media every 2 days for a total of 6 days. Cells will not proliferate during this period because of the absence of EGF and FGF2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S05 -->
6. Change media every 2 days for a total of 6 days. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S06 -->

### 1 day

#### Branch B: Preparing cells for immunocytochemistry and quality control

1. i. After 6-7 days of maturation, remove media and wash 1X with prewarmed D-PBS. To fix cells, remove D-PBS and add ice cold 4% PFA prepared as described in Reagent setup. Transfer the plate to ice for 30 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S01 -->
2. ii. Wash 3X with cold PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** PAUSEPOINT: Plates can be stored at 4°C for up to one month or used immediately. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S03 -->
3. iii. Proceed with immunocytochemistry with standard techniques to determine regional patterning efficiency and stage of differentiation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S04 -->

### 30+ days

#### Astrosphere maintenance and maturation

1. By day 90, astrospheres are primarily composed of cells with the ability to generate S100β+ immature astrocytes. Up to this stage, cells are maintained as spheres in order to easily select out any non-neural cells that attach to the flask. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S01 -->

### day 15

1. At day 15, when multiple rosette formations are present throughout the neuroepithelial (NE) culture, lift attached clusters. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S33 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note that non-neural colonies with absence of rosette formation should be mechanically removed before lifting the neural colonies to avoid contamination with non-neural cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S34 -->
2. To lift, exert a force upon the clusters with a 1 ml pipette until they detach, without breaking excessively into single cells. Flat, non-neural cells that migrate on the outer edge of the colonies should remain attached to the plate because of their higher degree of attachment. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S35 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Critical: Minimize breaking up the neural colonies at this stage for maximum cell survival. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S36 -->
3. Transfer floating aggregates to a 15-ml conical tube and centrifuge for 2 minutes at 100g, a speed used for all subsequent steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S01 -->
4. Remove old media (supernatant) by vacuum and resuspend the aggregates with prewarmed NM. Typically, from one 6-well plate of neuroepithelial cells, resuspend into 24 ml of NM. If morphogens are to be added to the culture system, dilute them into NM before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S02 -->
5. Using a pipette, transfer 8 ml of resuspended aggregates into each of three T25 flasks. Different sized flasks may be used if desired. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Critical: The neuroepithelial aggregates tend to stick on the inside of the pipette which results in a decreased yield. Therefore, rinse the pipette with media before transferring the aggregates to avoid losing spheres. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S04 -->
6. Every 2-3 days, replace media with fresh prewarmed NM +/- morphogens by tilting the flask to allow floating aggregates to settle to the bottom. Remove 75% of old media with a sterilized glass Pasteur pipette and replace with fresh NM +/- morphogens. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T2-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Critical: Clusters attached lightly to the flask should be lifted during addition of new media, simply by swirling the flask. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T2-S02 -->
7. If clusters are firmly attached or cells form a monolayer, only transfer the floating aggregates to a new flask and discard the attached cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T2-S03 -->

### day 21

1. On day 21, replace media with NM + EGF and FGF2 (10 ng/ml each) to expand the spheres. Morphogens are no longer necessary at this late stage for regional patterning. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T3-S01 -->
2. As described above, 75% of media is replaced every 2-3 days and spheres tightly attached to the flask should be discarded during exchange of new flasks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T3-S02 -->

### After 6-7 days of maturation (step B)

1. After 6-7 days of maturation, remove media and wash 1X with prewarmed D-PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T5-S01 -->
2. To fix cells, remove D-PBS and add ice cold 4% PFA prepared as described in Reagent setup. Transfer the plate to ice for 30 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T5-S02 -->
3. Wash 3X with cold PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T5-S03 -->
4. PAUSEPOINT: Plates can be stored at 4°C for up to one month or used immediately. Proceed with immunocytochemistry with standard techniques to determine regional patterning efficiency and stage of differentiation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T5-S04 -->

### By day 90

1. By day 90, astrospheres are primarily composed of cells with the ability to generate S100β+ immature astrocytes. Up to this stage, cells are maintained as spheres in order to easily select out any non-neural cells that attach to the flask. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T7-S01 -->
